req.title: Create task
req.statement: The system shall create a new task and respond with HTTP 201 and the created task body when POST /tasks/ receives a valid TaskCreate payload.
expected_outcomes: response body includes id, title, completed=false

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates POST /tasks/ returns HTTP 201 with id, title, completed=false in the body for valid payloads. I design: (1) a positive EP test with a fully valid payload asserting exact status 201 and all required fields; (2) a negative NEG test with a missing required field (title) asserting exact 422 status; (3) a BVA boundary test with title at exactly 1 character (minimum allowed by Field min_length=1); (4) a BVA boundary test with title at exactly 100 characters (maximum allowed); (5) a BVA boundary test with title at 101 characters (one over maximum, must be rejected); (6) a DT test with completed=true explicitly supplied, verifying the field is stored as provided; (7) a NEG test with an empty title string (violates min_length=1). These cover mutation operators: status-code constant mutations (201->200, 201->204), boolean field mutations (false->true), boundary off-by-one mutations on string length constraints, and missing-field validation path mutations.

tests.name: test_create_task_valid_payload_returns_201_with_required_fields
preconditions: Database is initialized with pre-loaded rows
actions: POST /tasks/ with valid JSON body: title='Buy milk', description='From the store', completed=false
expected: Response body contains field 'id' with an integer value
Response body field 'description' equals 'From the store'
trace: R-TASK-001: system shall respond HTTP 201 with created task body
Catches status-code mutation 201->200, boolean mutation completed false->true
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_create_task_valid_payload_returns_201_with_required_fields():
    payload = {"title": "Buy milk", "description": "From the store", "completed": False}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body["id"], int)
    assert body["title"] == "Buy milk"
    assert body["completed"] == False
    assert body["description"] == "From the store"
    assert "created_at" in body

tests.name: test_create_task_response_id_is_unique_across_calls
preconditions: Database is initialized with 20 pre-loaded rows
expected: The two returned ids are different integers
Each id is greater than 20 (pre-loaded rows occupy ids 1-20)
trace: R-TASK-001: each created task has a unique id
STC: state transition from 20 existing tasks to 21 then 22; catches mutation that returns constant id
tests.executable:
from app.main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app)

def test_create_task_response_id_is_unique_across_calls():
    r1 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task Alpha"})
    r2 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task Beta"})
    assert r1.status_code == 201
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    id1 = r1.json()["id"]
    id2 = r2.json()["id"]
    assert isinstance(id1, int)
    assert isinstance(id2, int)
    assert id1 != id2
    assert id1 > 20
    assert id2 > 20
